items.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
items.q: The interviewee mentions Kepard only in the context of the interviewer's questions and general discussion of other musicians (Freddie Kepler, Louie, Joe Sutler). There is no statement from the interviewee indicating a personal relationship, collaboration, or direct interaction with Kepard.

ctx.x: Freddie was. How did they compare in that day? Did people think of Louie as being better? Or

Kepard as being better? Freddie was the favorite. And for Louie establishing. So Louie started, I think the first tune to make Louie was West End. And from then on, Louie came into his own and he started recording. But prior to this, Freddie Kepler had Chicago. And then Joe Sutler.
Joe Sutler you think could match pretty close to Kepler? Yeah, pretty close. And then Louie, Louie stepped up where we're both up. Yeah. He was recording. Strange that Sutler never got
